1024.title: Expand model export format support
1024.body:
# Expand model export format support

> **Updated 2026-07-30** — re-audited against `develop` @ `c3294a5` (version `1.9.0`). Since this issue was opened, the TFLite runtime failure has been fixed, TensorRT has been promoted to a first-class `format=`, and ExecuTorch + native CoreML have landed. Original text preserved where still accurate; per-format sections now cite the PR that added the capability and the release that shipped it.

## Context

RF-DETR now exposes five first-class export formats through `RFDETR.export(format=...)`. This issue audits the broader CV deployment ecosystem, records current coverage on `develop`, and tracks the remaining gaps.

Industry-share figures below are directional estimates, not precise telemetry — they aggregate signals from the Ultralytics export ecosystem, ONNX/TensorRT/CoreML deployment surveys, edge-AI framework reviews, and visible community usage.

## Current state in `develop`

Verified by inspection of `src/rfdetr/export/` and `RFDETR.export()` in `src/rfdetr/detr.py`:

- `RFDETR.export(format=...)` accepts `"onnx"` (default), `"tflite"`, `"tensorrt"` (alias `"trt"`), `"executorch"` (alias `"pte"`), and `"coreml"` (`detr.py:1431`).
- `src/rfdetr/export/` is now a package with per-backend subpackages: `_onnx/`, `_tflite/`, `_tensorrt.py`, `_executorch/`, `_coreml/`, plus a shared `ExporterProtocol` in `protocols.py` and dispatch in `_backend.py`.
- **The TFLite runtime failure flagged in the original issue is resolved.** Fixed by #1041 (onnx2tf 2.4) and #1054 (ONNX-level GridSample rewrite), both released in **1.7.0**; numerical parity with `predict()` closed by #1131 in **1.8.2**.
- TensorRT is no longer a `--tensorrt` CLI post-step shelling out to `trtexec` — it builds through the TensorRT Python API via `polygraphy` (#853, **1.9.0**).
- TorchScript remains in-process only via `optimize_for_inference(compile=True)` → `torch.jit.trace`. Not a saveable export format. Unchanged.
- Optional dependency groups in `pyproject.toml`: `[onnx]`, `[tensorrt]`, `[tensorrt-bench]`, `[tflite]`, `[executorch]`, `[coreml]`.
- Unreleased on `develop`: `output_name` + unified artifact naming across all backends (#1250).

## Overview

| Format | Status on `develop` (1.9.0) | Added by | Released in | Est. industry share | RF-DETR architectural risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **ONNX** | ✅ First-class | pre-existing | — | ~30% (server) | Low — `F.grid_sample` exports cleanly |
| **TensorRT** | ✅ First-class `format="tensorrt"` | #853, #1231 | 1.9.0 | ~30% (server) | Low — no custom plugins |
| **TFLite / LiteRT** | ✅ Functional (FP32/FP16/INT8) | #920, #1041, #1054, #1131 | 1.7.0 / 1.8.2 | ~30% (edge) | Medium — GridSample rewrite carries the path |
| **ExecuTorch** (umbrella) | ✅ First-class `format="executorch"` | #1142 | 1.9.0 | ~3–5% (edge, growing) | Medium — fixed batch only |
| ├ `backend="xnnpack"` | ✅ Portable CPU, fp32 | #1142 | 1.9.0 | — (spans all edge CPU) | Low |
| ├ `backend="coreml"` | ✅ ANE/

1555.title: Explore temporal feature caching for faster video inference
1555.body:
### Search before asking

- [ ] Confirm that no existing issue covers this request before submitting.

*This check remains unconfirmed in the draft.*

### Description

Could we explore an optional video-inference mode that **reuses backbone calculations between consecutive frames**, updating regions that have changed rather than recomputing everything?

The [current forward path](https://github.com/roboflow/rf-detr/blob/develop/src/rfdetr/models/lwdetr.py) runs the image through the backbone and then the decoder. The proposed exploration would introduce reuse across frames, primarily inside the backbone, while keeping the decoder unchanged initially.

This is a feasibility request, not a proposal for a drop-in LLM-style KV cache. The question is whether **temporal feature reuse—including, potentially, attention keys and values—can reduce actual inference latency with an acceptable accuracy trade-off**.

### Use case

Real-time detection on continuous video streams, particularly fixed-camera or low-motion scenes where much of the image changes little between frames.

The goal would be to produce detections on every frame with less computation, rather than simply skipping frames. A useful evaluation should also cover camera movement and newly appearing objects, not just easy, mostly static scenes.

### Additional

#### Possible scope

| Stage | What to explore, in plain English | Initial role |
|---|---|---|
| **Backbone: attention keys and values** | Recalculate these intermediate values only for regions selected for an update. | A narrow comparison experiment. |
| **Backbone: broader intermediate features** | Reuse additional feature-processing results for regions with little change, rather than caching only keys and values. | Main direction to investigate. |
| **Decoder and prediction heads** | Run normally on every frame using the updated and cached backbone output. | Keep unchanged initially. |

Caching only keys and values would still leave the attention calculation and feed-forward processing to run unless those operations are also modified. This is why broader feature reuse seems worth comparing against KV-only caching.

Relevant code: [DINOv2 backbone with windowed attention](https://github.com/roboflow/rf-detr/blob/develop/src/rfdetr/models/backbone/dinov2_with_windowed_attn.py).

#### Important limitation

The DINOv2 backbone implementation includes windowed and full-image attention. Consequently, an unchanged patch of pixels can still acquire different internal features when something elsewhere changes.

**A pixel-difference mask alone would not guarantee valid feature reuse.** The prototype should therefore treat reuse as potentially approximate and evaluate how errors accumulate.

#### Suggested exploration

1. **Profile the baseline.** Identify which backbone operations dominate runtime and where selective updates could actually avoid work. The update decision should happen before the expensive calculation—not after running the full

Hi! We have finetuned a RFDETR-small model for object detection of a single custom class. In most cases it works very well, but there's an environment in which the model frequently outputs two detections for a single ground truth object in the image that have a very high IOU (>0.9). Our use case involves object counting so this is a breaking issue.

Specifically, We have trained a RFDETR-small model (with `rfdetr=1.3.0`) exported the model to onnx (opset 16) and are doing inference via a [Triton inference server (v2.49)](https://github.com/triton-inference-server/server/releases/tag/v2.49.0) with `onnxruntime=1.18`.

The obvious answer is to apply NMS postprocessing to resolve this, but since not requiring NMS (and the inference speed gain is brings) is one of the selling points of using RFDETR over YOLO I was wondering to what degree this is expected behavior or not! The expected number of detections per image for our use case is limited (<20) so the the NMS overhead would be minimal as well.

905.title: ONNX inference support in predict() and better export naming
905.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the RF-DETR [issues](https://github.com/roboflow/rf-detr/issues) and found no similar feature requests.


### Description

Two improvements to the ONNX workflow:

**1. Export naming** — Currently `model.export()` always saves as `inference_model.onnx` regardless of variant. Exporting RFDETRNano and RFDETRMedium to the same directory overwrites the file. The filename should include the variant name (e.g. `rfdetr-nano.onnx`, `rfdetr-medium.onnx`).

**2. ONNX predict** — After exporting a model to ONNX, there's no built-in way to run inference with it. Users have to handle preprocessing, ONNX Runtime session management, and postprocessing on their own. `predict()` should work with ONNX files directly, returning the same `sv.Detections` output as the PyTorch path.

Proposed workflow:
```python
# Export — filename includes variant
model = RFDETRMedium()
model.export(output_dir="output")  # → output/rfdetr-medium.onnx

# Inference with ONNX — same API as PyTorch
model = RFDETRMedium(weights="output/rfdetr-medium.onnx")
detections = model.predict("image.jpg", threshold=0.5)
```

### Use case

Anyone deploying RF-DETR with ONNX Runtime currently has to write their own inference code with duplicate preprocessing and postprocessing logic. This makes it harder to move from training to deployment.

With built-in ONNX predict:
- Same `predict()` API works for both PyTorch and ONNX models
- Returns `sv.Detections` regardless of backend
- Enables lighter deployment without the full PyTorch dependency
- Lays the groundwork for future backend support (TensorRT, OpenVINO)

### Additional

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [x] Yes I'd like to help by submitting a PR!

ONNX-TF only supports up to opset 13 for some operators (like Where), but
Your model uses operators (like aten::scaled_dot_product_attention) that are only supported in ONNX opset 14 or higher.
Summary of your situation:

If you export with opset 13: PyTorch cannot export your model because it uses newer operators.
If you export with opset 16: ONNX-TF cannot convert your model because it does not support some ops at that version.

1599.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the RF-DETR issues and found no similar bug report.


### Bug

Hi,

I am observing a strong sensitivity of **RF-DETR Segmentation confidence scores to very small translations of the input image**.

My original images are high resolution, so I need to split them into **512 × 512 tiles with 0.25 overlap** before training and inference.

The main issue is that the predicted **masks and bounding boxes remain correct**, while the classification confidence can change dramatically after shifting the same image by only a few pixels.

---


## Problem

For the same 512 × 512 tile, I apply small integer translations:

```text
dx, dy ∈ [-24, +24] pixels
```

The translation is applied before RF-DETR preprocessing.

Important details:

- integer pixel translations
- no interpolation during the shift
- reflection padding
- objects near image borders are excluded
- the same object is matched using IoU
- inference threshold during the sweep is `0.001`

A typical result can look like:

```text
dx =  0 px  -> confidence ≈ 0.91
dx =  1 px  -> confidence ≈ 0.90
dx =  2 px  -> confidence ≈ 0.86
dx =  3 px  -> confidence ≈ 0.79
...
dx = 11 px  -> confidence ≈ 0.49
dx = 12 px  -> confidence ≈ 0.88
dx = 13 px  -> confidence ≈ 0.86
...
dx = 24 px  -> confidence ≈ 0.89
```

In more extreme examples I have seen confidence change approximately from:

```text
0.80 -> 0.003
```

after only a small translation.

---

## Localization remains stable

The surprising part is that the localization usually remains correct.

For the same shifted object I can still obtain approximately:

```text
bbox IoU ≈ 0.90 - 0.95
mask IoU ≈ 0.90 - 0.95
```

while the classification confidence changes substantially.

Conceptually:

```text
Original:
correct bbox + correct mask + confidence 0.90

Shifted a few pixels:
correct bbox + correct mask + confidence 0.05
```

So this looks mainly like a **classification-confidence instability**, rather than a localization failure.

---

## Apparent periodic behaviour

The confidence changes also show an approximately **8 pixel periodicity** in the original 512 × 512 tile coordinates.

My configuration is:

```text
Tile size:             512 × 512
RF-DETR resolution:    768 × 768
Resize factor:         1.5
Patch size:            12 model pixels
```

Therefore:

```text
12 / 1.5 = 8 input pixels
```

This appears to match the observed period quite closely.

Because of this, I suspect the behaviour may be related to the patch/token grid, positional encoding, or the interaction between resizing and patch alignment.

I am not claiming this is definitely the root cause, but the correlation seems significant.

---

## Evaluation methodology

For each selected validation object:

1. Start from a baseline detection with confidence >= 0.80.
2. Require enough distance from the image borders.
3. Translate the image using integer `(dx, dy)`.
4. Run RF-DETR again.
5. Shift the expected bounding box by the same `(dx, dy)`.

1631.title: Half-precision keypoint trace fusion returns NaN scores for finite predictions
1631.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the RF-DETR issues and found no similar bug report.

#1192 fixes a later score-normalization overflow; this failure occurs earlier in the covariance trace calculation.

### Bug

Finite keypoint predictions can produce a NaN detection score during float16 inference. A subsequent `scores > threshold` comparison drops the detection. With the same inputs, float32/float64 return a finite score above the threshold. Bfloat16 also loses reduction precision in this example.

In `_keypoint_log_mean_trace`, `sigmoid(-20)` rounds to zero in float16. The `1e-12` clamp floor also rounds to zero, so both weighted `logsumexp` terms become `-inf`; their subtraction returns NaN.

The precision-Cholesky parameters in the reproduction represent identity covariance, whose trace is 2. Equal findability weights cancel in the mean, so the expected log trace is `log(2)`. With object logit 4 and the default `trace_alpha=0.2`, the expected normalized score is approximately 0.460885.

### Environment

- RF-DETR `1.12.0.dev` from develop at `2cdb8cd7db249a2919e3964631b96102aecd0d72`. The affected file is unchanged on current develop `8cb29175f1710eabc651ddcfa23e13c685ac6a5e`.
- Windows 11, Python 3.13.3, PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu for the reproduction and focused tests.
- I also ran this reproduction using the exact `PostProcess` class source from the latest release tag, `1.11.2`, with identical results in that CPU environment. This was source execution, rather than a separate installed-wheel test.
- CUDA helper checks and timings: PyTorch 2.11.0+cu130, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Laptop GPU.

### Minimal reproducible example

This needs no model download. All supplied model-output values are finite.

```python
import torch
from rfdetr.models.postprocess import PostProcess

for dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16, torch.float32, torch.float64):
```

- [x] I have searched the RF-DETR [issues](https://github.com/roboflow/rf-detr/issues) and found no similar bug report.

### Bug

Running `evaluate()` with the pretrained Nano on COCO val2017 gives 48.0 mAP, while the README lists 48.4. I recorded the exact predictions the metric callback scored and ran them through pycocotools too:

### Bug

### What happens

`pip install rfdetr[tensorrt]` resolves to TensorRT 11 today — the extra declares `tensorrt>=8.6.1`
with no upper bound. On TensorRT 11, `build_engine(..., fp16=True)` logs one warning, **exits 0, and

|---|---|---|---|
| `build_engine(fp16=True)` | 119,688,644 | **0.00** | **8.407** |
| same graph cast to FP16, built strongly typed | 65,059,180 | 86.87 | **2.170** |

**3.87× slower** than the FP16 the caller asked for. Anyone benchmarking RF-DETR against other
detectors publishes an FP32 latency labelled FP16.

Build log — the downgrade is visible, but non-fatal:

[INFO]    rf-detr - Building TensorRT engine (fp16=False) from /content/export/rfdetr-small.onnx

[I] Saving engine to /content/export/rfdetr-small_fp32.trt     <- exit 0

```python
1541.title: TensorRT export: a missing `tensorrt` is only reported after the ONNX export, and a dynamic-batch ONNX builds a batch-1 engine
1541.body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I have searched the RF-DETR issues and found no similar bug report.


### Bug


Two problems in `format="tensorrt"` / `TensorRTExporter.build_engine` on `develop @ 1985300a`.

**1. A missing `tensorrt` is only reported after the ONNX file has been written, with the wrong advice.**

`pip install "rfdetr[onnx]"` installs [Polygraphy](https://pypi.org/project/polygraphy/), which imports `tensorrt` lazily. So `_IS_TENSORRT_AVAILABLE` (`src/rfdetr/export/_tensorrt/exporter.py:57`) is `True` on a host with no TensorRT, and `_require_tensorrt()` (`:826`) checks a polygraphy symbol, not `tensorrt`. `RFDETR.export(format="tensorrt")` runs the full ONNX export first. Only then does it fail, inside Polygraphy, which suggests auto-installing instead of `pip install rfdetr[tensorrt]`:

```
[INFO] rf-detr - Successfully exported ONNX model to: out/rfdetr-nano.onnx
[INFO] rf-detr - Converting ONNX model to TensorRT engine
[!] Module: 'tensorrt' is required but could not be imported.
    Note: Error was: import of tensorrt halted; None in sys.modules
    You can set POLYGRAPHY_AUTOINSTALL_DEPS=1 in your environment variables to allow Polygraphy to automatically install missing modules.
polygraphy.exception.exception.PolygraphyException: Module: 'tensorrt' is required but could not be imported.
```

The existing check also sits inside `build_engine`, after `OnnxExporter` has run (`exporter.py:719` vs `:771`). So even when it does fire (polygraphy missing too), the user has already paid for the ONNX export.

**2. A dynamic-batch ONNX file built without `dynamic_batch` silently becomes a batch-1 engine.**

On the documented path for converting an already-exported `.onnx` (`docs/exports/tensorrt.md`, "Python API Conversion"), `build_engine` passes no optimization profile unless `dynamic_batch=True` (`exporter.py:890-894`). Polygraphy then fills every `-1` dimension with 1 and only warns, and rfdetr reports success:

```
[W] Input tensor: input (dtype=DataType.FLOAT, shape=(-1, 3, 384, 384)) | No shapes provided; Will use shape: [1, 3, 384, 384] for min/opt/max in profile.
[INFO] rf-detr - Successfully built TensorRT engine: dyn/rfdetr-nano_fp32.trt
# engine inspected afterwards with tensorrt.Runtime: get_tensor_profile_shape("input", 0)
[(1, 3, 384, 384), (1, 3, 384, 384), (1, 3, 384, 384)]
```

The engine then rejects every batch other than 1 at runtime. The opposite mismatch (`dynamic_batch=True` on a static graph) already raises a `ValueError` (`exporter.py:929-933`). `RFDETR.export(format="tensorrt")` is not affected, since it passes one `dynamic_batch` to both stages; only direct `build_engine` callers are.

**Why CI does not catch either.** CPU CI installs neither polygraphy nor tensorrt, so the unit tests fake the whole polygraphy chain, and the only dependency test patches `engine_from_network = None`. The GPU TensorRT job always installs both packages. No test builds a dynamic ONNX without `dynamic_batch`.
```
